adiabatic-lapse-rate.title: Lapse Rate
adiabatic-lapse-rate.info: The rate at which rising air cools as it expands under falling pressure — about 9.8°C/km dry, gentler once cloud forms. Pandora's weak gravity and heavy, heat-rich air flatten it, keeping the floating mountains green where an Earth peak would be bald ice.

albedo.title: Albedo
albedo.info: The fraction of starlight a surface bounces back to space instead of absorbing. Bright ice and cloud run cool; dark ocean and forest run warm. Together with distance from the star, albedo sets how much energy a world keeps to warm itself.

atmospheric-disequilibrium.title: Disequilibrium
atmospheric-disequilibrium.info: An atmosphere held far from chemical equilibrium, with gases that should destroy each other coexisting. Only a living planet can pump them faster than they react — Lovelock's test for life, read from four light-years off.

atmospheric-general-circulation.title: Circulation
atmospheric-general-circulation.info: The planet-scale system of air currents that carries heat from the hot equator toward the cold poles through linked overturning cells — Hadley, Ferrel, Polar. This machine, not chance, decides where a world is wet and where it stays dry.

carbon-chauvinism.title: Carbon Chauvinism
carbon-chauvinism.info: Astrobiology's reminder not to assume all life must be carbon-based like Earth's — with the twist that carbon really is thermodynamically superior. The skill is telling what chemistry genuinely forces from a mere habit of imagination.
carbon-chauvinism.carbonWhy: Four flexible, stable bonds; its oxide is a gas you can exhale
carbon-chauvinism.siliconWhy: Bonds too weakly; its oxide is quartz — a solid, not a breath
carbon-chauvinism.nitrogenWhy: Versatile, but its chains fall apart in water
carbon-chauvinism.phosphorusWhy: Vital in small roles, too reactive as a backbone
carbon-chauvinism.sulfurWhy: Useful cross-links, but poor at long stable chains
carbon-chauvinism.boronWhy: Rare and awkward, with a scarce cosmic supply

carbonate-silicate-cycle.title: Carbon Thermostat
carbonate-silicate-cycle.info: Earth's long-term thermostat: CO₂ weathers rock, the sea buries it as carbonate, subduction cooks it, volcanoes exhale it. Weathering speeds up when warm, so the loop self-corrects — the resolution of the faint-young-sun paradox.

coriolis-effect.title: Coriolis Effect
coriolis-effect.info: The apparent sideways deflection of moving air and water caused by a planet's spin — right in the north, left in the south. It bends winds into east-west streams and breaks circulation into cells. It never touches your bathtub drain.

daisyworld.title: Daisyworld
daisyworld.info: Lovelock and Watson's toy planet: black and white daisies that warm or cool their own patch. As the sun brightens they rebalance, holding temperature nearly flat — regulation with no regulator, the answer to the teleology objection.

earth-system-science.title: Earth Systems
earth-system-science.info: The discipline treating Earth as one coupled system of rock, water, air, and life — Gaia grown up. It keeps the defensible core of coupled feedbacks and drops the teleology: just negative feedbacks found, named, and quantified.
earth-system-science.tapArrow: Tap an arrow to trace a coupling
earth-system-science.e_bioAtm: Life floods the air with oxygen
earth-system-science.e_atmCryo: A warming atmosphere melts the ice
earth-system-science.e_cryoAtm: Bright ice reflects sunlight and cools the air
earth-system-science.e_hydAtm: The ocean stores and moves the planet's heat
earth-system-science.e_lithAtm: Volcanoes exhale CO₂ from the rock
earth-system-science.e_atmLith: Acid rain weathers the silicate rock

gaia-hypothesis.title: Gaia Hypothesis
gaia-hypothesis.info: Lovelock and Margulis's idea that Earth's biosphere, air, oceans, and crust form one tightly coupled system holding conditions fit for life. Its strong form — a planet that regulates itself like an organism — is the lens for reading Pandora.

great-oxidation-event.title: Oxidation Event
great-oxidation-event.info: The turning point ~2.4 Gyr ago when photosynthetic cyanobacteria pumped out enough free oxygen to remake Earth's air from a reducing haze into the reactive mixture we breathe — proof a biosphere can transform an entire planet's air.

hadley-cell.title: Hadley Cell
hadley-cell.info: The largest loop of circulation: warm air rises at the equator, rains into rainforest, drifts poleward, and sinks as dry desert air near 30°. Slower spin widens it — which is why slow-turning Pandora is rainforest coast to coast.

homeostasis.title: Homeostasis
homeostasis.info: A system holding a stable internal state against a changing outside, always through a negative feedback loop. Your body at 37°C, a planet holding its climate — the Na'vi call it keeping the balance of life.

intertropical-convergence-zone.title: ITCZ
intertropical-convergence-zone.info: The belt around the equator where trade winds meet and force warm moist air up, raining almost daily — which is why the densest rainforests track it. On slow-spinning Pandora the rain belt broadens into a vast tropical band.

negative-feedback.title: Negative Feedback
negative-feedback.info: A loop where a change triggers a response that opposes it, pulling the system back toward stability — the engine of all self-regulation. Too little gain crawls back; too much overshoots and rings.

partial-pressure.title: Partial Pressure
partial-pressure.info: The share of pressure one gas contributes to a mixture — its fraction times the total (Dalton's law). Your lungs read the push, not the percentage, so the same 21% oxygen is breathable at sea level yet suffocating atop Everest.

positive-feedback.title: Positive Feedback
positive-feedback.info: A loop where a change amplifies itself, driving the system further from its start. Below gain 1 it dies; above 1 it runs away. This is the mechanism behind tipping points — a small warming turned irreversible.

radiative-equilibrium.title: Radiative Balance
radiative-equilibrium.info: The state where a planet radiates exactly as much energy as it receives, holding its temperature steady. Albedo and greenhouse set where the balance lands; Pandora's dense air lifts the surface far above the bare baseline.

superrotation.title: Superrotation
superrotation.info: When a world's whole atmosphere spins far faster than the surface beneath it — Venus and Titan do it. A slow-spinning, dense-aired world like Pandora drifts toward it, spreading heat evenly around the globe.

thermohaline-circulation.title: Thermohaline
thermohaline-circulation.info: The ocean's great heat conveyor, driven by density that temperature and salinity together set. Cold salty water sinks and upwells elsewhere. On Pandora tidal heat warms the seafloor, favouring rich local upwelling.

tipping-point.title: Tipping Point
tipping-point.info: A threshold where a small change triggers a large, abrupt, often irreversible shift to a new state — one the system then defends just as stubbornly. Cross the crest and stabilising feedbacks give way to runaway ones.

claw-hypothesis.title: CLAW Hypothesis
claw-hypothesis.info: An ocean feedback (Charlson-Lovelock-Andreae-Warren): warm the sea, plankton bloom and vent sulphur that seeds bright cooling clouds. Push too far and the plankton collapse instead, and the loop flips from brake to runaway.
claw-hypothesis.runawayFlip: Plankton collapse — the loop flips to runaway

wind-layer-router.title: Which River Are You In?
wind-layer-router.subtitle: A caravan cannot fight the wind — it can only choose a height
wind-layer-router.staffAria: A vertical wind staff: barbs at each altitude point the way that layer flows, short and westward near the ground, long and eastward in the jet aloft
wind-layer-router.mapAria: Ground track produced by drifting for {days} days at the chosen level

hint.surface: Down here friction drags on the air, slowing it and twisting its heading away from the flow above. You go west, slowly, and you can see the ground — which is why caravans launch from this layer and rarely trade in it.
hint.trade: The steady low easterlies: reliable, moderate, and pointed west. A caravan that never climbs will circle the moon in this layer, the long way round, and arrive at every rendezvous late.
hint.middle: The wind here is weak and its heading unreliable — the layer between the two conveyors, where a caravan makes almost no progress in any direction. Navigators cross it; they do not linger in it.
hint.westerly: Above the reversal the flow has swung the other way and strengthened. This is the working level for an eastbound leg: fast enough to matter, calm enough to hold formation.
hint.jet: The core. Four times the speed of the trades, and almost due east — a caravan that finds it crosses in days what the low layer takes a season to cover. The price is the climb, and the turbulence at its edges.

jet-meander.title: When the Sky Stops Arriving
jet-meander.subtitle: A jet meanders; sometimes the meander stands still

aria.progressive: A gently waving jet band travelling steadily eastward past a stationary caravan
aria.stalling: A sharpening jet band creeping slowly across the map, nearly stationary
aria.blocked: A large, deeply buckled jet band locked in place over the caravan

hint.progressive: The flow carries the pattern east faster than the wave can propagate west, so troughs and ridges sweep past. Weather keeps arriving, and a caravan can wait a few days for the layer it wants.
hint.stalling: The two speeds are close to cancelling. The pattern has slowed to a crawl and begun to amplify — the sky a navigator watches nervously, because whatever is overhead now may still be overhead next week.
hint.blocked: The wave has gone stationary and buckled. A stalled high sits over the caravan, the jet has split around it, and there is no fast layer to climb into. This is the failure mode that strands a fleet: not a storm, but a sky that has stopped moving.

ballast-budget.title: Five Legs, One Account
ballast-budget.subtitle: Every climb spends water; every descent vents gas; neither comes back

hint.arrived: That itinerary works. Notice what it required: not the fastest layer everywhere, but the right layer on each leg, bought with a water and gas budget that had just enough in it. This is what a navigator's memory is actually for.
hint.short: The account survived, but the caravan fell short. Progress is not about finding one good altitude — the fast layer moves as you travel, so a fleet that holds a single level spends most of the crossing in air going the wrong way.
hint.stranded: The caravan asked for a level it could no longer afford and had to hold the one it was already in. Out here that is not an inconvenience; it is the end of the route. Ballast spent early is control you do not have later.

ballast-budget.startNote: The caravan launches from the {level} layer, so choosing anything else for the first leg already costs a climb.

season-reversal.title: Why Twice a Year
season-reversal.subtitle: The circuit is quick; the wind's permission is not
season-reversal.aria: A ring of one Pandoran year divided into {reversals} wind seasons, the flying share of each drawn bright and the moored remainder dim
season-reversal.mooredNote: moored, trading, waiting for the turn
season-reversal.overrunNote: the wind turns before the circuit closes

hint.fits: The crossing fits inside one wind season with time to spare — and that spare time is the trading. The rhythm is not set by how fast a caravan can travel but by how often the wind grants a direction, which is exactly the logic that paced the monsoon dhows.
hint.overruns: At this speed the circuit cannot close before the wind reverses, and a caravan caught mid-route by the turn is a caravan pushed back the way it came. Fewer, longer seasons are more forgiving than many short ones.
